ActionClosed.title: ActionClosed
ActionClosed.description:
`already` says the item was resolved before this call, so a second
click is not reported as a second resolution.

AdminMailEvent.title: AdminMailEvent
AdminMailEvent.description:
One classification, as written. The log is append-only, so a message
with three of these was corrected twice and the last one is in force.

AdminMailMatch.title: AdminMailMatch
AdminMailMatch.description:
One match attempt, with the application it named. Append-only as well,
so a tier that keeps being corrected stays visible as history rather than
being papered over one row at a time.

AdminMailMessage.title: AdminMailMessage
AdminMailMessage.description:
The stored message, whole, for the one surface that may see everybody's.

The columns were a `SELECT *`, so what reached the client was whatever the
table happened to hold on the day. `body_html` is the markup as it
arrived: the user-facing reader sanitises on read, this one does not,
because an administrator debugging a classification needs what the
classifier saw.

Answer.title: Answer
Answer.description:
`_ANSWER_COLS`, in types. `turns` is the back-and-forth, oldest first:
the person's edits and instructions and the model's rewrites, each with a
role, a kind and a time.

ApplicationAction.title: ApplicationAction
ApplicationAction.description:
An open ask, and what could ever close it without a person.

`settles_on` is `mail_pipeline.settles_on`, not a second reading of it: an
empty list means nothing that arrives can close this item, which is a
different thing from an item still waiting, and such an item must not be
rendered as a live obligation.

ApplicationEvent.title: ApplicationEvent
ApplicationEvent.description:
One event reaching an application, through the message it was read from.

The row `events_for` and `events_by_application` both select, declared
once because a list and a detail view disagreeing about an application's
events is worse than either being wrong alone. `stage_for` reads `kind`
and `id`; everything else is what a reader needs to check the stage
against the mail that produced it.

ApplyContext.title: ApplyContext
ApplyContext.description:
The three sources a fill draws from, before anything is filled.

`profile` is a map rather than the profile shape: only the facts that are
set are listed, because a blank fact fills nothing and listing it would
say the profile has something it does not.

ApplyReport.title: ApplyReport
ApplyReport.description:
How the ladder is doing on this person's submitted forms. `by_rung`
is keyed by the rung that filled the field, with "blank" for the ones
nothing filled.

ArmResult.title: ArmResult
ArmResult.description:
One arm's answer for one posting. `output` is shaped by the step being
measured.

Assignment.title: Assignment
Assignment.description:
One of three targets. An application to attach to, a board job to
create an application from, or a company and title when neither exists -
which is the common case for mail predating the catalog.

Attached.title: Attached
Attached.description:
What still hangs off a source, and therefore what deleting it would
orphan.

Autofilled.title: Autofilled
Autofilled.description:
What the write filled in that the caller did not send.

A status change can date the row by itself, so the caller is told rather
than having to re-read the row to find out.

An absent key is the answer, not a null: the route sets
response_model_exclude_none so `{}` still means "nothing was filled",
which is what the board already reads. Declaring the shape must not move
the wire.

BatchRecord.title: BatchRecord
BatchRecord.description:
A batch as stored. `prompt_id` is the prompt version it was submitted
under, which is what makes a batch's answers attributable to a prompt
rather than to a model alone.

BatchedCheck.title: BatchedCheck
BatchedCheck.description:
One verdict this batch produced. `est_cost_usd` is not stored: it is
priced here from the batch's model at the batched rate, so a batch is
inspectable down to what each individual request cost.

note.title: Note
note.default: Missing batch IDs do not establish synchronous transport. unrealized_savings_usd is a legacy half-cost scenario, not verified savings.

BatchingDiagnostics.title: BatchingDiagnostics
BatchingDiagnostics.description:
A retained compatibility estimate. Missing batch IDs do not prove
synchronous transport, which is why the basis travels with the numbers.

Board.title: Board
Board.description:
One page of the board, and everything the page needs to render its own
controls without re-deriving them.

BoardAnalytics.title: BoardAnalytics
BoardAnalytics.description:
One board.

`configured` is false for a source that has supplied postings and has no
catalog row. `funnel` is keyed by check name rather than declaring one
field per check, because the checks are a registry (core.checks) and a
model enumerating them would be the literal that registry exists to
remove; the `custom` key carries the wider shape.

BoardAnalyticsList.title: BoardAnalyticsList
BoardAnalyticsList.description:
`caveats` ships with the numbers rather than beside them on a wiki,
because a caveat a reader has to go and find is one that will be missed.

BoardDecay.title: BoardDecay
BoardDecay.description:
`dead_on_arrival` is the FIRST closed-check on a posting already saying
closed: what the board handed over. `still_open` is the latest verdict:
what has died since.

BoardDrill.title: BoardDrill
BoardDrill.description:
Where the frontend goes to see the rows behind a number, built on the
server so the filter that produced an aggregate and the filter that
fetches its members cannot drift apart.

`checked_jobs` is deliberately the funnel denominator and not the posting
count: /v1/admin/jobs aggregates ai_queries and only knows postings that
have a verdict.

BoardFreshness.title: BoardFreshness
BoardFreshness.description:
Age comes from `date_posted`, never from `created_at`: created_at is
when a row was loaded into this catalog and the whole table shares a floor
from the last reseed. `with_date_posted` therefore reports how much of the
board these ages actually cover.

BoardIngest.title: BoardIngest
BoardIngest.description:
`last_success_at` is when the pull last ran cleanly.
`freshness.last_loaded_at` is when it last produced a posting this catalog
had not seen. The gap between the two is a board serving a frozen feed.

BoardInventory.title: BoardInventory
BoardInventory.description:
How many postings this board has supplied, and how many it still calls
live.

`active_share` is comparable only between boards with the same
`reports_inactive`. False means nothing this board ever supplied is marked
inactive, which means its feed has no way to say otherwise - a fact about
the feed's format, not about the board.

BoardOptions.title: BoardOptions
BoardOptions.description:
Everything the board's filter and edit controls need, generated from
data instead of hardcoded in the client.

`ats` here is the board-wide count, the profile of the board as a whole.
The per-page counts under the other filters are `facets` on the list.

BoardOverlap.title: BoardOverlap
BoardOverlap.description:
Keyed on (company, title), because jobs.url is unique table-wide: a
posting belongs to exactly one source by construction, so duplication is
invisible at the url level.

BoardReliability.title: BoardReliability
BoardReliability.description:
How often this board's postings were already gone the first time they
were checked. An observation over `sample_n`, not a prediction.

BoardRow.title: BoardRow
BoardRow.description:
`_JOB_ROW`, in types: the posting, the ATS read off its url, and this
person's own row over the top.

`closed_verdict` is three-valued and must stay that way: 'open', 'closed',
or null for never checked. `active` cannot answer this question, it is
whatever a board's feed last said and nothing ever clears it.

BoardSpend.title: BoardSpend
BoardSpend.description:
What this board's postings cost to check, as billed at the time.

`window` is in the response because /admin/spend defaults to 30 days and
this takes no window at all, so a reader comparing the two was comparing a
lifetime against a month with nothing saying so. All-time is right here:
whether a board earned its keep is a question about its whole life.

Not split per check_type: verify_new books one batched call against the
`closed` row and writes the clearance verdict from the same response, so a
split would read as though clearance were free on some paths.
`priced_coverage` keeps "this cost nothing" apart from "we do not know what
this cost".

BoardStatusCount.title: BoardStatusCount
BoardStatusCount.description:
`status` is 'not_applied' where the row has none, so every board row is
counted under some heading.

BoardYield.title: BoardYield
BoardYield.description: What the board's postings became once a person saw them.

BootstrappedUser.title: BootstrappedUser
BootstrappedUser.description:
Who the caller is, as the session already knows them. Empty rather than
null where the identity provider sent nothing, which is what AuthedUser
already holds.

Breakdown.title: Breakdown
Breakdown.description:
One bucket of rejections. `examples` is a reproducible sample of
`distinct_phrasings`, not a frequency ranking; see `_finish`.

BulkPatchResult.title: BulkPatchResult
BulkPatchResult.description:
`skipped` names the ids the caller may not touch rather than refusing
the whole selection: a selection made from the board can include a row
that vanished or was never theirs, and failing everything for one would
send the page back to a request per row.

CandidateApplication.title: CandidateApplication
CandidateApplication.description:
One application this message could belong to, and why it is on the list.

`reason` separates a candidate the matcher considered and declined to
choose between from a search hit. A dismissed application is listed so the
picker can show it and refused at the write, so `dismissed_at` is part of
the row rather than a reason to omit it.

CandidateJob.title: CandidateJob
CandidateJob.description:
A posting on the board with no application yet. Attaching mail to one
creates the application, which is the correction people most often want.

CandidateMessage.title: CandidateMessage
CandidateMessage.description:
The message the picker is deciding about, with what the classifier read
out of it - which is what the ranking below compared.

CatalogCounts.title: CatalogCounts
CatalogCounts.description:
What a dashboard tile needs. `by_kind` counts active sources per board
format; `last_ingest` counts sources by how their most recent pull ended.

CatalogSource.title: CatalogSource
CatalogSource.description:
A source row as stored, plus the format read off its URL. `kind` is
never a column: it is derived from `listings_url` every time, so it cannot
drift from what ingest will do with the row.

CheckRerun.title: CheckRerun
CheckRerun.description:
The verdict the re-run produced, and what produced it. `check` echoes
what was asked for, which is not always `check_type`: filter:<id> and
hash:<prompt_hash> both run as a custom check.

CheckStage.title: CheckStage
CheckStage.description:
One check's latest verdict per posting, counted.

`coverage` is how much of the board the stage has seen at all: a pass rate
over 2% of a board says almost nothing about the other 98%.

CheckVerdict.title: CheckVerdict
CheckVerdict.description: The latest verdict for one posting check.

CheckedPosting.title: CheckedPosting
CheckedPosting.description:
Every check ever run against one url, rolled up. The company and title
are MAX() over the rows rather than a join to the catalog: this is the
verdict ledger's own account of a posting, and it answers for urls the
catalog no longer holds.

`verdict` is the roll-up of the roll-up: one rejection anywhere makes the
posting rejected, since a posting that fails any check is out.

ClassificationCell.title: ClassificationCell
ClassificationCell.description:
What one model said, at one confidence, about how many messages - with
the two things that go wrong inside a correct-looking answer: no company
extracted, and a deadline the model inferred rather than read.

ClassifiedLocation.title: ClassifiedLocation
ClassifiedLocation.description:
A list row, which also says when it was classified. The PUT does not
return this field, so the two shapes are two models rather than one with
a field that is sometimes there.

ClassifiedLocations.title: ClassifiedLocations
ClassifiedLocations.description:
`total` counts what the filters keep; `total_all` counts the whole
table, so the page can say "40 unplaced of 12,000" without a second
request.

Company.title: Company
Company.description:
One company NAME, not one company. `company_key` is
lower(btrim(company)) over free text, so spelling variants are separate
rows and a distinct-name count is an upper bound on the number of real
employers.

`applications`, `open` and `repost` are null when the name is below the
floor that would make them mean anything, and so is `responses` inside the
first. The server stays the single authority on what is well powered; a
caller renders a null block as nothing at all and never computes the floor
itself.

They were ABSENT rather than null until this was declared. Dropping them in
a serialiser keeps that wire and erases the schema - pydantic derives it
from the serialiser's return type, so the model becomes an open object,
which is the generated type this phase exists to stop producing. So the
null wins, and the consumers are checked instead.

CompanyApplications.title: CompanyApplications
CompanyApplications.description:
The calling user's applications under this name, counted from
`applications` and not from the board: the board only knows postings
tracked by hand, while `applications` also holds the ones only email knows
about.

`statuses` is still what the user typed on the board, so an application
with no board row counts in `n` and in no status - a real gap between what
mail knows and what he has recorded, left visible rather than reconciled
away.

CompanyCoverage.title: CompanyCoverage
CompanyCoverage.description:
A company that has not replied may simply not have been READ yet.
Silence is only evidence once the mailbox is classified, so the size of the
backlog travels with the numbers that depend on it rather than being
something a reader has to know to ask about.

CompanyExtraction.title: CompanyExtraction
CompanyExtraction.description:
Named for what the extractor did, because that is all these three can
honestly claim. They sum to total_postings_seen.

CompanyList.title: CompanyList
CompanyList.description:
`total_names` counts what the lenses show rather than the whole catalog:
same CTEs, same cuts, no page. `next_cursor` is an offset and says so.

CompanyOpen.title: CompanyOpen
CompanyOpen.description:
The latest closed verdict per posting, the same instrument the board row
and the per-job signal use. Null below OPEN_MIN_CHECKED, which is where
"9 of 14 still answer" stops being worth a sentence.

CompanyPay.title: CompanyPay
CompanyPay.description:
`measures` and `not` travel WITH the number rather than in the
response-level caveats, because a caveat one refactor away from the datum
it qualifies is a caveat that will eventually be dropped. A posting that
stated pay we failed to read is indistinguishable from one that stated
none, so `n_extracted` is a count of what we found, never of what this
employer discloses.

CompanyRepost.title: CompanyRepost
CompanyRepost.description:
One title repeated under several urls on a SINGLE source AT ONE
LOCATION, more than signals.REPOST_MIN_SPAN_DAYS apart.

Location is in the key because without it a chain listing one role across
its estate reads as one enormous repost. This is the largest surviving
group, so `url_count` is reported: a high count is an evergreen
requisition, not a repost cycle.

CompanyResponses.title: CompanyResponses
CompanyResponses.description:
Does this company reply, and how long does it take?

RATES ARE ALMOST ALWAYS NULL HERE, and that is the honest answer rather
than a defect: of 1,283 companies with an application, 449 have two, 87
have five and TWO have thirty. The numerator and denominator carry the
information and the caller renders "2 of 7". A company with three
applications and one reply does not have a 33% response rate; it has one
reply.

A reply is any classified mail. `reached_outcome` counts only the mail that
DECIDED something - an acknowledgement is a mail server saying it received
the form, and counting it would report a 100% response rate for every
company running an ATS.

ConsistencyCoverage.title: ConsistencyCoverage
ConsistencyCoverage.description:
What the rate is a rate OF. Only a repeated body can be checked this
way, so this is a canary over part of the corpus and never a measure of
it - a rate quoted without this would describe a canary as a census.

ConsistencyGroup.title: ConsistencyGroup
ConsistencyGroup.description: One body the classifier saw more than once, and the answers it gave.

ContentMix.title: ContentMix
ContentMix.description:
Where a source's check text came from over the last week. ATS text is
free and scraped text is paid for, so a source sliding from one to the
other is a cost change nothing else reports.

ContextDraft.title: ContextDraft
ContextDraft.description:
A draft already written for this posting. Only drafts that exist are
listed, so `draft` is never null here.

CorrectedJob.title: CorrectedJob
CorrectedJob.description:
The catalog row as the correction left it. Only the fields a person may
correct come back, plus the url and id that identify which row moved.

CostBasis.title: CostBasis
CostBasis.description:
What a cycle cost is computed FROM, so the client can render it as an
estimate with its basis rather than as a price. per_cycle is the handler's
own cap; a task with no cap sends 0 and no cycle cost.

CurrencyRange.title: CurrencyRange
CurrencyRange.description:
What our extractor read, per currency it read it in.

Currency is present on 452 of 11,442 extracted rows, so a null currency is
the ordinary case and gets its own entry rather than being folded into USD:
an amount whose currency was never captured is not a dollar figure.

CurrentMatch.title: CurrentMatch
CurrentMatch.description:
The match row in force for a message.

Declared beside the query that reads it, because an admin correction
returns it verbatim and the columns were a `SELECT *` - so what reached
the client was whatever the table happened to hold. A null
`application_id` is a recorded outcome rather than an absence: `method`
says which of the two it is.

CustomCheckStage.title: CustomCheckStage
CustomCheckStage.description:
Custom filters are per user and one posting can be judged by several,
so there are two honest denominators and both are here. `checked` and
`pass_rate` are job-level - a posting passed every filter it was put in
front of - and `evaluations` counts the judgements behind them.

DataHealth.title: DataHealth
DataHealth.description:
`suppressed` is always empty and is kept deliberately: a detector that
is off and says nothing is indistinguishable from a detector that sees
nothing, so a future suppression has somewhere to be reported.

DayTotals.title: DayTotals
DayTotals.description:
One calendar day in the session timezone, not the first ten characters
of a timestamp.

DeferredPulls.title: DeferredPulls
DeferredPulls.description:
The pulls waiting on a slot for one host, so the page can say "3
waiting, next 14:52" without paging every pending ingest task.

reason.title: Reason
reason.default: user_job_working_set has no admission timestamp, so newly admitted digest candidates cannot be reconstructed

DigestComparison.title: DigestComparison
DigestComparison.description:
Legacy non-force candidates and unclassifiable proposed rows.

`cannot_tell` is the number of working-set rows with no admission time. It
is not a proposed candidate count.

DomainPopulation.title: DomainPopulation
DomainPopulation.description:
The sender breakdown is also TRUNCATED, so it says how many domains it
shows against how many exist.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description:
What a match actually rested on.

The rationale says what the matcher concluded; this says what it concluded
it FROM. The company the classifier read out of the mail is what tiers 2
and 3 compared, so if that extraction is wrong the match is wrong and no
amount of staring at the conclusion reveals it.

EvidenceCriterion.title: EvidenceCriterion
EvidenceCriterion.description:
What "evidence missing" means, in the payload rather than in whoever
explained it once.

ExamplesSelection.title: ExamplesSelection
ExamplesSelection.description: How the examples were chosen, for the same reason.

ExcludedStage.title: ExcludedStage
ExcludedStage.description:
A stage left out, said out loud. A number quietly missing is worse
than one that names why it is not here.

Experiment.title: Experiment
Experiment.description:
`_COLS`, in types. `params` is the request as it was made (arms,
sample, seed) and `summary` is what scoring made of the answers; both are
shaped by the step being measured, which is why neither is declared
further.

ExperimentIndex.title: ExperimentIndex
ExperimentIndex.description: The runs, plus what a form needs to make a new one.

ExperimentQueued.title: ExperimentQueued
ExperimentQueued.description:
The run as stored, plus the task that will carry it out and the arms
that were asked for and cannot run. An arm is refused for a reason the
caller can act on, so it is returned rather than dropped.

Explained.title: Explained
Explained.description:
One check re-run on purpose, with the reasoning the cheap path skips.

`refetched` and `closure_signal` are present only when the content could
not be fetched and the fetch itself said why: a 404 or a removal notice is
an answer about the posting, not a failure to get one.

Facets.title: Facets
Facets.description:
Counts under every OTHER filter the page has on. Taken before the ats
clause joins the rest, because a board-wide "rippling 4" beside a lens
that holds none of them reads as a lie.

FailedCheck.title: FailedCheck
FailedCheck.description:
One failure behind a pivot row. `error` is the first 300 characters:
a driver traceback is longer than the screen and the cause is at the front.

FailureBreakdown.title: FailureBreakdown
FailureBreakdown.description:
`items` is empty unless the request named a worker or a host: the
pivot is the whole fleet, and the individual failures are a drill-down.

FailurePivot.title: FailurePivot
FailurePivot.description:
Failures grouped by the worker that ran them and the host they were
fetched from. `host` is read off the url, so a row with no url has none.

Field_.title: Field_
Field_.description:
One field as the extension read it. kind is the widget: text, long,
select, yesno, file, number, date. options are the select's choices
as shown, in order.

Fill.title: Fill
Fill.description:
One pass of the extension over one form. `job_id` is null when the url
matched no posting on the board, which is normal rather than an error.

FilterPreset.title: FilterPreset
FilterPreset.description:
A preset as stored: a prompt somebody can start a filter from, shared
across everyone rather than owned by one person.

FilterRow.title: FilterRow
FilterRow.description:
A filter as the list shows it: the run in flight for this one, and
whether another may start.

FilterRunQueued.title: FilterRunQueued
FilterRunQueued.description:
`ignore_budget` is echoed because it is the whole reason this route
exists beside the person's own: the run is going past the shared weekly
cap, and the answer says so rather than leaving it to the request.

FilterVerdictRow.title: FilterVerdictRow
FilterVerdictRow.description:
One of this person's filters, and how it last judged this posting.
Everything but the filter itself is null when it has never run on it.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description:
What a detector raised, before it was written to a row. The same four
fields health_alerts stores, with no id: a finding that matches an alert
already open updates it rather than opening a second.

FleetBudget.title: FleetBudget
FleetBudget.description:
Where fleet spend sits against its ceiling, with what the ceiling does
not cover carried as data rather than left in a comment.

FleetWorker.title: FleetWorker
FleetWorker.description:
One worker, as its heartbeat and its current task leave it.

`alive` is the heartbeat being under 90 seconds old, resolved in SQL so
every reader agrees on the same clock. The task fields are null when the
worker is idle: they come from a join on a task that is still running.

FormState.title: FormState
FormState.description:
Whether this job's form could be read, and what came back. `questions`
is a count, because the questions themselves are merged into the answers
above rather than listed twice.

FunnelStage.title: FunnelStage
FunnelStage.description:
One stage with its own denominator. `reached` counts applications an
event of that kind ever arrived for, so the stages overlap and do not sum
to `of`.

GmailStatus.title: GmailStatus
GmailStatus.description:
The grant as the settings page renders it. `available` is about the
caller's groups and the rest is about the grant, which is why an
unavailable mailbox is still a 200 with connected=false.

Grants.title: Grants
Grants.description: What this person may spend and on what, in one place.

GroupApplied.title: GroupApplied
GroupApplied.description:
Every board the person now holds, not just the bundle's, because
"replace" keeps boards that are switched off and "add" keeps everything.

GroupBreakdown.title: GroupBreakdown
GroupBreakdown.description:
A bucket that a taxonomy group named. The residual bucket is the same
shape without the name, and rides on the row as `ungrouped`.

GroupBudget.title: GroupBudget
GroupBudget.description:
What a group may spend on the shared key. A null budget is uncapped and
null allowed_models is every model in the catalog; both are real answers
rather than unset ones.

GroupBudgets.title: GroupBudgets
GroupBudgets.description:
`catalog_models` is every model the server can run, so the form offers
a closed list rather than a text box that fails on save.

GroupGrant.title: GroupGrant
GroupGrant.description:
A group this person is in that carries a budget. A null budget is
uncapped, which is a real answer and not a missing one.

HealthAlert.title: HealthAlert
HealthAlert.description:
An open or recently resolved alert.

`subject_kind` is not a column. It says WHAT the subject is - a source, a
host, a provider and user, a task kind - and is annotated on read from the
one map in api.health, so an alert opened before the map existed still
gets the right answer. It is null for a kind the map does not name.

`detail` is whatever the detector that raised the alert had to show, so
its shape is that detector's and is not declared further.

HealthRun.title: HealthRun
HealthRun.description:
`open` is everything the detectors found; `new` is how much of it was
not already open, which is what would have been notified.

HostBudget.title: HostBudget
HostBudget.description:
The pace one egress address keeps against one board host, as the fleet
has learned it.

`closed` means the next slot is in the future, which is ordinary pacing.
`blocked` is the different thing: refused repeatedly with nothing ever
accepted, so no gap will open it. It is computed on read rather than
stored, so the rule lives in one place (api.hosts.blocked).

ImprovedPrompt.title: ImprovedPrompt
ImprovedPrompt.description:
What the model wrote, and what it says it changed. The same shape it
is asked for and the shape this route returns, because there is nothing
in between.

InFlight.title: InFlight
InFlight.description:
The task a person is waiting on, as the page shows it.

Declared here rather than in the router that surfaces it, because the
columns are this function's and a router copying them is how the two
drift. `filter_runs` finds its own conflicting task with its own query
and returns this same shape, which is why `kind` is here: it was already
in that query, and one model for one idea beats two that agree today.

IngestQueued.title: IngestQueued
IngestQueued.description:
What was queued, and what was already being pulled. A board already in
flight is reported rather than queued twice; the request only fails when
every board named was in flight and nothing was queued at all.

IngestTotals.title: IngestTotals
IngestTotals.description:
The same counts summed over every board, so the page need not add up
751 rows to show a headline.

Ingesting.title: Ingesting
Ingesting.description:
The pull queued or running for a board, so the page can disable its
button from server state rather than guessing.

Invite.title: Invite
Invite.description:
An outstanding invitation, as Authentik holds it. `pk` is Authentik's
id and is what revoking one names.

InviteCreated.title: InviteCreated
InviteCreated.description:
`emailed` is false when the invite was created but delivery failed, so
the link is returned either way and somebody can send it by hand.

InviteList.title: InviteList
InviteList.description:
`configured` is false when the Authentik environment is missing, which
is why the list is empty rather than there being nothing outstanding.

JobDetail.title: JobDetail
JobDetail.description:
Everything behind one board row: the posting, the content that was
judged, this person's own row and its history, and why the checks and
filters let it through.

JobFacts.title: JobFacts
JobFacts.description:
The posting behind one board row. Wider than `BoardRow` where the
detail view needs it and narrower where the list does.

LedgerBucket.title: LedgerBucket
LedgerBucket.description:
One grouping set of the usage ledger. The three below are the same
measures cut three ways, so the dimension each carries is the only thing
that differs.

LedgerTotals.title: LedgerTotals
LedgerTotals.description:
Lifetime totals over every model call. `cost_usd` is not a column: it
is the sum of what each model's tokens priced at, and a model that cannot
be priced contributes nothing to it rather than a guess.

LedgerWithTotals.title: LedgerWithTotals
LedgerWithTotals.description:
The ledger with the two populations' totals side by side. They answer
different questions and stay labelled rather than forced to agree.

LocationPut.title: LocationPut
LocationPut.description:
One place through country/region/city, or several through places;
places wins when both are sent.

MailCorpus.title: MailCorpus
MailCorpus.description:
The whole import, deliberately NOT windowed: how much mail exists, when
it starts, and how much nothing has looked at are properties of the
import rather than of a slice.

MailEvent.title: MailEvent
MailEvent.description:
One classification of this message, as written. The log is append-only
and the newest wins, so a message with three of these was corrected twice.
A null `model` is how a human correction is told apart from a model's.

MailList.title: MailList
MailList.description:
The page, plus what it was sorted and filtered by.

`sortable` and `filterable` are the vocabulary a client builds its controls
from, and `sorts`/`filters` echo what was actually applied, so the page
never has to duplicate the default or guess the keys.

MailMatchRow.title: MailMatchRow
MailMatchRow.description: One attempt to place this message, with the application it named.

MailMessage.title: MailMessage
MailMessage.description:
One of a person's own messages: what arrived, what it was read as, and
where it went.

Not the debug row. An admin asks which messages the pipeline handled
badly and needs the prefilter and the model; a person asks what arrived
and which application it reached.

MailMessageDetail.title: MailMessageDetail
MailMessageDetail.description:
The whole message with its history, for when the excerpt is not enough.

Read-only and user-scoped. The body is already stored - withholding it
would mean leaving for a mail client to check a decision this system
made, which is the same as not being able to check it.

MailRow.title: MailRow
MailRow.description:
One message as the debug list shows it: what arrived, what the
classifier last said, and what the matcher last did with it.

Every field after `prefilter_reason` is the CURRENT row of an append-only
log and can be null for its own reason - no classification yet, no match
attempted, a match that found nothing. They are not interchangeable and
`_where` filters on the difference.

ManagedBoard.title: ManagedBoard
ManagedBoard.description:
A sponsor-owned board definition.

``on_ambiguous=filter`` excludes postings whose criteria result is
ambiguous; ``keep`` retains them.

Market.title: Market
Market.description:
What the roles this user is targeting ask for. Every count is against
`postings`, the size of the slice, because a share hides how thin a slice
is: "3 of 7" and "43%" read the same and mean very different things.

`skills` is keyed by skill kind, which `core.requirements.SKILL_KINDS`
defines, so an empty slice still answers with every kind present.

MarketFlags.title: MarketFlags
MarketFlags.description:
Counts of postings that SAY something, reported beside `postings`
rather than as shares, for the same reason.

MatchMoved.title: MatchMoved
MatchMoved.description:
Which message the correction moved. The append is on the MESSAGE, so
the id says what changed hands rather than restating the application the
caller already named.

MatchOverridden.title: MatchOverridden
MatchOverridden.description:
The match now in force, which is what the append produced rather than
what was asked for - a refusal is recorded as the matcher's own refusal
method, so agreeing with the matcher looks like agreeing with it.

MatchedPosting.title: MatchedPosting
MatchedPosting.description: The posting the url matched, when the board holds one.

MatchingCell.title: MatchingCell
MatchingCell.description:
How many messages of a kind the matcher settled, and by which tier.
`never attempted` is a method value here because an absence in a
distribution is a gap nobody can read.

MeasurableModel.title: MeasurableModel
MeasurableModel.description:
A chat model an experiment may name, with the efforts it accepts. The
runner refuses the rest, so the form only offers these.

Mention.title: Mention
Mention.description:
The whole message, and where the company appears in it.

Offsets rather than a highlighted string, so the client decides how to
mark it and the body stays exactly what the sender wrote. `start` is null
when the company does not appear verbatim, which is common: the classifier
reads it off a signature or a logo as often as out of a sentence.

MessageAssigned.title: MessageAssigned
MessageAssigned.description:
What the assignment wrote. `messages_assigned` is how many moved: one
click that quietly reassigns a dozen messages should report it rather than
have the count discovered later.

ModelCandidate.title: ModelCandidate
ModelCandidate.description:
One model this task could run on, eligible or not, carrying WHY.

Every dollar figure is a decimal string, never a number: these are
Decimals and a float would round money on the way out. None means unknown
- an ineligible model has no price and an unbounded sweep has no cycle
cost - and rendering either as 0 would make an unknown look like a free
one.

ModelChangeEffect.title: ModelChangeEffect
ModelChangeEffect.description:
What happens to work already done when this task's model changes.

Declared rather than inferred, because it is a fact about the handler's
candidate query and nothing here can see one. Getting it wrong on a screen
is worse than omitting it: the two answers point in opposite directions.

ModelEvidence.title: ModelEvidence
ModelEvidence.description:
A measured finding about one model on this task, carried as data so the
client renders it on the option it is about rather than holding its own
copy that rots at the next measurement.

ModelHealth.title: ModelHealth
ModelHealth.description: The same record on the screen, with the window it was measured over.

ModelSpend.title: ModelSpend
ModelSpend.description:
`model` is null for the scrape-only checks, which record an attempt
rather than a judgement and carry neither a model nor a cost.

ModelTotals.title: ModelTotals
ModelTotals.description:
What one model has been asked and what that cost.

The batched columns are carried because batched and synchronous tokens
bill at different rates and are priced as two calls: one blended rate over
the whole model would be wrong by up to 2x depending on the mix.

`cost_usd` is null where the model cannot be priced from summed tokens: a
tiered model's rate depends on each individual request's prompt length, so
a thousand small calls sum into a tier none of them was billed at, and the
honest answer is that it is not priced.

MyPromptVersion.title: MyPromptVersion
MyPromptVersion.description:
The same prompt version as its owner sees it: their own filter names
rather than every name the prompt has been given, and no owner block,
because they are it.

NewSourceRequest.title: NewSourceRequest
NewSourceRequest.description:
The receipt for a board someone asked for. Narrower than the row the
list returns: a request a moment old has no resolution, and shipping the
resolution fields as nulls would say it was looked at and left.

Ok.title: Ok
Ok.description:
It worked and there is nothing to say about it.

Returned where the interesting outcome is the status code. A route with
something to report returns that instead; this is not a wrapper to put
around a real answer.

OverlapPartner.title: OverlapPartner
OverlapPartner.description: Another board carrying the same (company, title) as this one.

OwnRow.title: OwnRow
OwnRow.description:
This person's own row, which is null when they have never touched the
posting. A board row is a grant as well as a record, so absence is a real
answer rather than an empty one.

OwnedFilter.title: OwnedFilter
OwnedFilter.description: A filter that carries this prompt today.

PatternPreview.title: PatternPreview
PatternPreview.description:
What a candidate pattern would admit, against every title this board
has listed. `would_add` is screened titles it lets in, `would_drop` is
catalog titles it turns away. Nothing is written.

PendingKind.title: PendingKind
PendingKind.description:
What is waiting, and how long the oldest of it has waited. The age is
what turns a pending count into "something is stuck".

Phrasing.title: Phrasing
Phrasing.description: One distinct rejection sentence, with how often it was written.

PhrasingPage.title: PhrasingPage
PhrasingPage.description:
`filters` echoes what narrowed this page, keyed by parameter name, and
carries only the parameters that narrowed anything.

PipelineAction.title: PipelineAction
PipelineAction.description:
The same item on the list, which names the application it is about
because the list has no application in hand.

PipelineApplication.title: PipelineApplication
PipelineApplication.description:
The row plus everything derived from the mail about it.

Nothing here is stored. `stage` is recomputed from the events on every
read, which is what makes a late or reclassified message correct itself
rather than need repairing, and `strongest_tier` is a property of the
MATCHES rather than of the application - matches are append-only, so a row
reports the strongest tier among its current ones.

PipelineDetail.title: PipelineDetail
PipelineDetail.description:
One application with everything that decided it.

The stored row, the stage derived from the events, and the events and
matches themselves. It carries the row's own fields rather than nesting
them, which is what the list row does too, so a client holding either
reads `company_name` the same way.

PipelineMatch.title: PipelineMatch
PipelineMatch.description:
The attempt, what it was decided FROM, and who decided it.

Without `evidence` a person has to open their mail client to check a
match, which is the same as not being able to check it. `corrected_by` is
derived rather than stored: the same actor id reads as "you" to the owner
and as an administrator to anyone else, so there is no second copy of that
distinction to drift.

PipelineStage.title: PipelineStage
PipelineStage.description:
The stage vocabulary in process order, with which stages are over, so
the lenses are read from here rather than copied into the client.

PipelineSummary.title: PipelineSummary
PipelineSummary.description:
Counts, not a funnel: terminal stages beat progress regardless of
arrival order and a stage is recomputed rather than advanced, so nothing
flows through anything.

Dismissals are counted rather than hidden. They change every other number
here, and a total that silently shrinks week to week with nothing
explaining why is the failure this whole system keeps producing.

PlacedLocation.title: PlacedLocation
PlacedLocation.description:
One classified location string, as the write left it.

The display columns are the FIRST place: a string naming three cities is
three entries in `places`, and `country`/`region`/`city` carry the first
of them so a list can show something without unpacking the array. A string
the model could not place has every one of them null.

Population.title: Population
Population.description:
The denominator a section counts over, and what it leaves out. Each
section below counts a DIFFERENT population and nothing in the rows says
so, which invites a subtraction that means nothing.

PostingAge.title: PostingAge
PostingAge.description:
How long this one listing has been up. Carries no sample size, because
it is a fact about this posting rather than a rate over many.

PostingClosed.title: PostingClosed
PostingClosed.description:
`reason` is what was recorded on the verdict, which is the admin's note
with who wrote it prefixed, not the note as sent.

PostingGone.title: PostingGone
PostingGone.description:
No re-run happened, because the re-fetch found the posting closed.

A separate shape rather than nullable fields on CheckRerun: nothing was
asked of a model here, so `model` and a token count would be a guess, and
`closure_signal` names what the fetch saw. `refetched` is always true,
since a closure can only be discovered by fetching.

job_related_a_gate_would_have_dropped.title: Job Related A Gate Would Have Dropped

PrefilterSummary.title: PrefilterSummary
PrefilterSummary.description:
A rate the prefilter could never report about itself, and the reason it
was kept as a signal rather than deleted: the mail a gate WOULD have
dropped is the one unrecoverable failure.

PresetCoverage.title: PresetCoverage
PresetCoverage.description:
Counts, not a rate. "170 of 7,397 already judged" is the sentence; a
percentage hides that the remainder is unjudged rather than rejected.

PresetOffer.title: PresetOffer
PresetOffer.description: A preset with what it would show today, so adopting one is not blind.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description:
A refusal a caller can branch on.

`code` is for the program: stable, greppable, and the thing a client
switches on. `message` is for the person, and may be reworded without
breaking anybody.

ProblemReport.title: ProblemReport
ProblemReport.description:
One row of the problem-report list, declared rather than implied.

The row shape used to reach the frontend as an untyped dict, so the types
on the other side were written by hand from reading this query. They
drifted: a capture field typed as a string was an object, and the page
crashed on 2026-09-10 when a report with fields was opened. A declared
shape puts that in openapi.json, which is where the frontend's types come
from.

ProblemReportDetail.title: ProblemReportDetail
ProblemReportDetail.description:
One report with the capture itself, which is the part triage reads.
The list above carries a title and a field count out of the same column
rather than the whole page.

ProblemResponse.title: ProblemResponse
ProblemResponse.description:
The wire shape. FastAPI wraps whatever `detail` holds in this key, so
a caller reads `detail.code`, not `code`.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.description:
Every fact a form asks that is not a question about the job. Blank
means unknown, and an unknown fact leaves its field blank rather than
guessing. EEO answers default to declining.

ProfilePut.title: ProfilePut
ProfilePut.description: Replace the whole profile; omitted fields return to their defaults.

PromptOwner.title: PromptOwner
PromptOwner.description:
Who holds this prompt, and whether it can still reject anything.

`state` is resolved, shared or unknown: a prompt that was edited or
deleted resolves to nobody, and 29% of rejections measured over the
corpus are in that state. `enabled` is null when no current filter
carries this prompt at all, because then there is nothing to ask.

PromptTotals.title: PromptTotals
PromptTotals.description:
`rejected_with_reason` is the denominator the groups are of, which is
not `rejected`: the batched paths recorded no reason for a stretch.

PromptVersion.title: PromptVersion
PromptVersion.description:
One prompt version, which is the unit here rather than one filter.

`sibling_hashes_by_name` is per name, not a single number: a hash can
carry several names, and a scalar would leave a caller unable to say
which name it describes.

ProposalAnswered.title: ProposalAnswered
ProposalAnswered.description:
What answering actually wrote.

`board_status` is present only when a row moved. It used to carry the
proposed status whenever the answer was `accepted`, including for the
applications with no board row where the UPDATE matched nothing, so the
caller was told a status had moved that no SELECT could find.

ProviderBatch.title: ProviderBatch
ProviderBatch.description:
One batch job at the provider, with the task it belongs to.

`requests` is what was submitted, `completed` and `failed_count` what came
back. `est_tokens` is what submission estimated; `input_tokens` and
`output_tokens` are what the provider billed, so the two disagreeing is
the estimate being wrong rather than anything being lost.

ProviderCosts.title: ProviderCosts
ProviderCosts.description:
What the provider says it charged, as reported now rather than a
finalized invoice. A window that could not be read whole reports its
reason and no total; it never reports zero.

QueryFilterOptions.title: QueryFilterOptions
QueryFilterOptions.description:
The dropdowns, generated from live data so they cannot drift from what
exists. `contexts` and `workers` are narrowed to the last 30 days: a value
nothing has produced in a month is a dead option, not a filter.

QueryListing.title: QueryListing
QueryListing.description:
`_LIST_COLS`, in types: one model call as the ledger lists it.

`instructions`, `input_content` and `parsed_json` are deliberately absent.
They are page dumps and prompts, several kilobytes each, and only the row
a person opens needs them; GET /admin/queries/{id} carries those.

`job_id` and `source` are looked up per row rather than joined: ai_queries
and jobs share several column names, so a join would make every existing
filter ambiguous. A verdict about a url the catalog no longer holds has
neither.

QueryRecord.title: QueryRecord
QueryRecord.description:
One model call, whole: what was asked, what came back, and what it
cost. `instructions` and `input_content` are the prompt and the page as
they were at the time, which is what makes a verdict re-readable rather
than merely re-runnable. `parsed_json` is the answer before it was reduced
to status and reason.

`cost_usd` is a float rather than a Decimal because a declared Decimal
serialises as a JSON string and this has always been a number.

QueryResponses.title: QueryResponses
QueryResponses.description:
Every model call against one url, whole rows, oldest first. This is the
drawer that shows what was asked and what came back, so it carries the
prompt and the page text the list deliberately leaves out.

QueryVocabulary.title: QueryVocabulary
QueryVocabulary.description:
The older, unscoped vocabulary: every distinct value ever recorded.
GET /admin/queries/options is the same idea narrowed to what is still in
use, and is what the queries page reads.

Question.title: Question
Question.description:
An answer as the application view shows it. A question the form
carries but nobody has drafted yet has no row, so every field but the
question itself is empty, and `multiline` says whether the box wants
prose.

QueuedTask.title: QueuedTask
QueuedTask.description:
One row of the queue. `payload` is the task's subject and `progress` is
what the handler has said about itself so far, both shaped by the kind, so
neither is declared further.

`cancellable` is not a column: it is whether the row's status is one a
cancel would reach, resolved on read so the page does not carry a second
copy of that list.

Rate.title: Rate
Rate.description:
A proportion carrying the counts that produced it.

`value` is null below the floor and the caller renders "2 of 7", so the
numerator and denominator are always present. `below_floor` says which
kind of null a null value is: too small a sample, or no trials at all.

RecheckOptions.title: RecheckOptions
RecheckOptions.description:
`defaults` is keyed by check option, not by check type: a re-check may
be asked for by filter id or prompt hash, and the person's last choice is
remembered against what they asked for.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: the canonical table, zlib-compressed and base64-encoded

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: sha256 of the canonical table; equals revision

RecipeConfig.title: RecipeConfig
RecipeConfig.description: What the extension fetches: the identity and the encoded table.

RecipePublished.title: RecipePublished
RecipePublished.description:
The revision now serving that adapter. A revision is derived from the
body, so publishing the same recipe twice returns the same one.

RecipeRevision.title: RecipeRevision
RecipeRevision.description:
One publish. The recipe body itself is not here: this is the history
list, and a body is tens of kilobytes that only the editor opens.
`bytes` is its size, which is what the list has a use for.

Reclassified.title: Reclassified
Reclassified.description:
What a correction moved. The affected applications come back rather
than an `ok`, because a changed kind can change what an application is
waiting for - including one the person is not currently looking at.

RememberedAnswer.title: RememberedAnswer
RememberedAnswer.description: One answer the bank kept from a submitted form.

ReportCreated.title: ReportCreated
ReportCreated.description: The extension shows the number, so the person can quote it.

ReportQueue.title: ReportQueue
ReportQueue.description:
`can_close_posting` tells the drawer this build has the close route, so
it offers the action rather than discovering a 404.

ReportedPosting.title: ReportedPosting
ReportedPosting.description:
A report somebody filed about a posting, with enough of the posting and
the person beside it that the queue reads without a second request.

`corrections` is what the reporter says the right answer is, shaped by the
kind of report, so it is not declared further. `posting_closed` is not a
column: it is the latest closed verdict for the url, which is what decides
whether the drawer offers to close it.

Repost.title: Repost
Repost.description:
The same title, at the same locations, listed more than once. Location
is part of the key: without it one chain listing a role across its estate
reads as one enormous repost.

RequestedSource.title: RequestedSource
RequestedSource.description:
A board somebody asked for, with who asked. `status` is open, added or
dismissed, and a resolved request keeps its row so the same board is not
added twice.

RequestedSources.title: RequestedSources
RequestedSources.description:
`total` counts the whole selection, not the page. The Requests badge
once showed the page size as the queue count.

ResolveApplication.title: ResolveApplication
ResolveApplication.description:
The application a row is about, with the stage the board would show.

`stage` is `mail_pipeline.stage_for` over that application's real events,
not a second reading of them, so the queue and the board cannot disagree
about what an application is doing while asking about it.

ResolveImplication.title: ResolveImplication
ResolveImplication.description:
What answering would change beyond the row itself.

Present only where there is something to say. A control whose effect
reaches past the row states that before the click rather than reporting it
afterwards, and `board_updated` is the honest half of that: an application
with no board row has a status to propose and nothing to move.

ResolvedField.title: ResolvedField
ResolvedField.description:
The field as read, plus what `resolve` decided about it.

Declared here rather than in the router that returns it, because the
three keys are this function's answer and a router that copies them is
how the two come apart. `rung` is which source filled it (profile, bank,
draft, resume) and is "" when nothing did; `hint` is the person's own
answer when the options did not recognisably hold it, which is what the
model is given instead of the value.

ResolvedForm.title: ResolvedForm
ResolvedForm.description:
What goes in each field, and what the extension needs to put it there.

`profile` is the whole profile as a map, minus the default resume and the
notes: a config-driven reader fills a repeated group one row at a time and
a selector that names another fact reads the scalar from it, so the keys
are read at runtime rather than known here.

ResolvedModel.title: ResolvedModel
ResolvedModel.description: What would run right now, and the grounds for it.

Resume.title: Resume
Resume.description:
`_RESUME_COLS`, in types. `text` is what the drafts are written from;
`pdf` is not here because the file is fetched from its own route.

ResumeFile.title: ResumeFile
ResumeFile.description:
The resume a fill would attach. `has_pdf` false means there is text to
draft from and no file to upload.

ResumeRef.title: ResumeRef
ResumeRef.description: Enough to choose one from a menu.

Reverted.title: Reverted
Reverted.description:
What restoring the model's answer moved.

`already` says the model's answer was already in force, and then nothing
was resynced - so `affected_application_ids` is absent rather than empty,
and the routes carry `response_model_exclude_none` to keep it that way. An
empty list would claim a recomputation that did not run.

RunDecision.title: RunDecision
RunDecision.description:
Whether a run may start now, said to whoever draws the button.

Declared here beside the decision rather than in the router that shows
it: `reason` is either why access was refused or IN_PROGRESS, and
`task_id` is the run already in flight when there is one, otherwise the
run this decision would start.

RunningTask.title: RunningTask
RunningTask.description:
A task a worker holds right now. `source` is lifted out of the payload
because an ingest is most of the queue and the board is what identifies
it; every other kind has none.

SavedFilter.title: SavedFilter
SavedFilter.description:
A filter as it stands after a write, with what the write set running.

`run_blocked` is why nothing was queued: a budget reason, or DEFERRED
when the hourly sweep will judge the board instead of this request.

SenderSignal.title: SenderSignal
SenderSignal.description:
What an application's first sender says about whether this is an
employer relationship at all.

A possibility, never a verdict: nothing filters or hides on this.
`sender_company_count` is the evidence and `review_suggested` is only a
reading of it, so both travel and the reader can disagree.

SettingsPut.title: SettingsPut
SettingsPut.description:
Partial settings update: omitted fields preserve their saved value.

Null resets column_layout, ai_model and writing_style to their defaults.
Other fields retain their legacy null-as-omission behavior. Supplied
objects replace the whole object; {} clears it, subject to the age cap
when criteria are written. False is a saved value, not an omission.

Rejects unknown keys rather than dropping them.

`background` was a key here until it was removed, and a client still
sending it needs to be told. Pydantic's default is to discard an
unrecognised key silently, which would answer 200 to a write that
stored nothing - the one failure a caller cannot detect.

Signals.title: Signals
Signals.description:
Every signal is null when it cannot clear its floor.

It used to be absent instead, because a caller renders "no signal" as
nothing at all and an empty object is a correct answer. Declaring the
shape made the keys appear with null, which the one consumer reads
identically: `!signals?.posting_age` is true either way. Null is kept
rather than serialised away because a key that is sometimes absent cannot
be typed, and being able to type it is the reason this exists.

What must not change is that a null here means the signal DOES NOT EXIST.
Never a zero, and never something for the caller to re-derive.

Source.title: Source
Source.description:
One board on the subscribe page. `enabled` is this caller's own
subscription and `kind` is derived from the listings url rather than
stored, so a board cannot say it is one fetcher while another reads it.

SourceBundle.title: SourceBundle
SourceBundle.description:
A named set of boards, so a person subscribes to "quant" rather than to
forty sources one at a time. `members` are source names.

SourceGroup.title: SourceGroup
SourceGroup.description:
A bundle of boards a person can take in one press. `subscribed` is
computed per caller rather than stored: the bundle is theirs only while
they hold every board in it.

SourceIngest.title: SourceIngest
SourceIngest.description:
One board over the window. The counts come from what each ingest task
left on its progress: `fetched` is what the board listed, `kept` is what
the title pattern admitted, `cached` is pages we already held, `gone` is
postings the board reports removed. `new_jobs` is catalog rows created,
which is the only one of these that is not a task's own account of itself.

A source that pulls fine and delivers nothing shows pulls with no
new_jobs, which last_new_posting_at alone cannot show for a mirror.

SourceLedger.title: SourceLedger
SourceLedger.description:
One row of the full list. `title_pattern` is deliberately absent: it is
a regex repeated on most rows and only the edit form reads it, through
GET /admin/sources/{name}.

`last_ingest_at` says the fetch worked. `last_new_posting_at` says the
fetch found something we had not already seen. The gap between them is
what retires a source.

SourceName.title: SourceName
SourceName.description:
The vocabulary a picker needs, and nothing that costs a join over
jobs.

SourceRequest.title: SourceRequest
SourceRequest.description:
A request with what an administrator did about it. Both fields are null
until someone answers, which is the difference between this and the
receipt the POST returns.

SourcesPatched.title: SourcesPatched
SourcesPatched.description:
What the delta actually did, beside what the person now holds. `added`
and `removed` are what the write touched, so a name already subscribed
reports as neither.

SourcesSwitched.title: SourcesSwitched
SourcesSwitched.description:
What was asked for, what the selection resolved to, and which rows
actually moved. `selected` and `changed` differ by the rows that already
held the value.

Spend.title: Spend
Spend.description:
Two populations, kept labelled: the usage ledger, and the verdict log.

Everything under `verdict_diagnostics` is repeated at the top level, which
is where the clients read it from. Nothing has moved; the nesting names
the population the numbers come from.

SpendWindow.title: SpendWindow
SpendWindow.description:
What the figures cover: the requested window, and the first and last
call actually inside it.

StatusCount.title: StatusCount
StatusCount.description:
A status and how many board rows carry it. The empty string is the
board's own name for "no status yet", not a missing value, which is why
the query coalesces rather than letting null through.

StatusMeta.title: StatusMeta
StatusMeta.description:
What a status MEANS, served beside the names so the board never decides
"is this over" or "which tone" by matching a name it hand-copied. A status
absent from the table is in play with no outcome.

StructuredOutput.title: StructuredOutput
StructuredOutput.description: How far a provider can be trusted to return a parseable object.

Submitted.title: Submitted
Submitted.description:
The ledger row after the person clicked submit.

An entry stays a map on purpose. It is the field as read, plus the final
value and whether it changed, plus whatever the model's pass left on it -
so naming the keys here would silently drop the ones it did not name.

Suggested.title: Suggested
Suggested.description:
The model's pass over what the ladder left blank. `answers` is keyed by
field key and holds only what came back usable; `skipped` is what the
admin list keeps from the model, which is not the same as unanswered.

Suggestion.title: Suggestion
Suggestion.description:
A proposal with what it rests on. The queue carries the summary
instead: the body is a detail view's worth of payload and there are 1,159
of these.

TaskModel.title: TaskModel
TaskModel.description:
One configurable task: what runs it, what else could, and what each
would cost.

TaskModelChange.title: TaskModelChange
TaskModelChange.description:
One decision, as the append-only table holds it. A cleared override is
a row with no model, not a deletion.

TaskProgress.title: TaskProgress
TaskProgress.description:
What `set_progress` writes: how far, out of how much, and a line for a
person. A handler may add counts it wants queryable afterwards (what an
ingest fetched, kept, cached, failed to fetch) and the health detectors
read those keys, so extras are carried rather than dropped.

The three have defaults because a parent task's progress is written by
`jsonb_set` on one key, and a row that has reported nothing should read as
nothing rather than fail the request that asks for it.

TaskQueue.title: TaskQueue
TaskQueue.description:
`summary` counts the whole selection, not the page, so a filtered view
says how much it matched rather than how much it drew.

`statuses` is the lifecycle in order, which is what lets the page render
them in that order rather than alphabetically.

TaskState.title: TaskState
TaskState.description:
A task this person started. Ownership lives in the payload, so the
kinds that stamp no user_id are fleet work with nobody to show them to.

TasksCancelled.title: TasksCancelled
TasksCancelled.description:
`skipped` names only ids the caller asked for by id and that were not
cancellable. A selection by kind or status cancels whatever matches, so
there is nothing for it to skip.

Thread.title: Thread
Thread.description:
The conversation, and whether it is all of it. A thread silently cut at
the cap reads as a conversation that ended, so the cut is said.

ThreadMessage.title: ThreadMessage
ThreadMessage.description:
One message of a conversation, with what the pipeline made of it.

Sanitised per message, same as the single-message reader: a thread is
where a person reads mail in context, so serving it as stripped text here
and as rendered mail one click away would be the same message in two
shapes.

ThreadSummary.title: ThreadSummary
ThreadSummary.description:
A conversation as a row: when it ran, who was in it, and whether it
still needs somebody.

`needs_attention` is the correctable pile - a thread carrying job-related
mail that reached no application. Not "unread": there is no such concept
here and inventing one would be a second inbox to maintain.

ThroughputBucket.title: ThroughputBucket
ThroughputBucket.description:
One hour of one worker on one kind. This is what makes a pending count
an ETA, so it is per worker and per kind rather than a fleet average.

TimeToOutcome.title: TimeToOutcome
TimeToOutcome.description:
How long this company took to decide something.

`basis` is tracker_dated_only, and that is not a caveat about precision.
For every mail-derived application `applied_at` IS the first matched
message's sent_at, so a duration over those measures the gap between the
first mail and the first DECIDING mail - zero whenever a rejection arrives
with no acknowledgement before it.

Median and p90 rather than a mean: over the 200 tracker applications with a
clean duration the mean is 30.5 days and the median 7.9, so the mean is
describing the tail rather than the wait. A median needs a sample as much
as a proportion does, so below the floor both are null and `n` carries what
there is.

TimelineEntry.title: TimelineEntry
TimelineEntry.description:
One check in a posting's history, thin enough to render as a line. The
interesting column is `reason`: a posting's story is the sequence of
verdicts and why each one was given.

Totals.title: Totals
Totals.description:
The bookkeeping rows, deliberately not the board. Counted from
user_jobs, so `tracked` includes rows whose posting has since left.

Tunable.title: Tunable
Tunable.description:
One registry entry, as `api.config.ConfigKey` holds it. `type` is the
name of a Python type rather than the type, because it travels as JSON and
the page only needs to tell an int box from a checkbox.

TunableWritten.title: TunableWritten
TunableWritten.description:
The value as stored, which is not always the value as sent: a spec
normalises what it validates, so the caller is told what landed.

Tunables.title: Tunables
Tunables.description:
The stored values beside the registry that describes them, both keyed
by the config key. `config` holds only keys app_config has a row for;
`keys` holds every key the registry declares, which is what lets the page
render one it has never seen.

Uploaded.title: Uploaded
Uploaded.description:
Accepted and rejected separately, with the reason on each rejection: an
upload is the one place a person chooses the url, so being told now beats
a job that silently never extracts.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description: The grants, with the spend they have been put to.

UsageCall.title: UsageCall
UsageCall.description:
One recorded call. A null cost means nobody looked the price up, never
that the call was free.

UserBudget.title: UserBudget
UserBudget.description:
Which cap applies to this person, resolved here rather than left to the
page. The Users page showed a weekly total one click from a page showing a
5,000,000 budget with nothing saying which cap applied to whom, which
invited the reading that an uncapped owner was over budget.

`owner_key` is whether they spend on the shared key at all; somebody on
their own key has no cap to be under.

UserDetail.title: UserDetail
UserDetail.description:
Everything one person's page shows: who they are, what they may spend
and what they have spent, what their board and filters look like, and the
last ten things the fleet did for them.

UserFilterRow.title: UserFilterRow
UserFilterRow.description:
A person's filters, without their prompts: this page is about who they
are, and the prompt is theirs to read on their own screen.

visibility_basis.title: Visibility Basis
visibility_basis.default: materialized board_visible rows; timestamps describe rows present, not projection freshness

UserJobsBulkPatch.title: UserJobsBulkPatch
UserJobsBulkPatch.description:
One patch for a selection. Same field vocabulary as UserJobPatch; the
cap keeps one request from holding a transaction over a whole catalog.

UserLedger.title: UserLedger
UserLedger.description:
`sort`, `dir` and `sorts` echo the sort that was applied and `sortable`
enumerates the keys, so the page renders the active sort without
duplicating the default and never has to guess what it may ask for.

UserLedgerRow.title: UserLedgerRow
UserLedgerRow.description:
One person, with the four counts the ledger sorts on. Each is a
correlated count rather than a join, so a person with no board rows and no
filters still appears with zeros.

`has_byo_key` says whether they hold their own provider key, which is what
decides whose budget their runs come out of. The key itself never leaves
the database.

UserMail.title: UserMail
UserMail.description:
The page, and the per-kind counts over the SAME predicate - so a tab's
number and its contents cannot disagree.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description:
A person and their settings, minus anything secret. `criteria` and
`ai_params` are shaped by what the person saved, so neither is declared
further.

UserSettings.title: UserSettings
UserSettings.description:
A person's saved settings, plus the two read-only fields the settings
page needs beside them: the built-in writing style it uses as a
placeholder, and what will actually run.

UserSettingsSaved.title: UserSettingsSaved
UserSettingsSaved.description:
The write's answer: the settings as GET serves them, and that it took.

The deployed page read criteria off this response to decide whether a
criterion was supported, found no criteria in {"ok": true}, and told
Kanishk his include list was unsupported by an API that had just stored
it.

VerdictDiagnostics.title: VerdictDiagnostics
VerdictDiagnostics.description:
The verdict log's own view of spend, labelled apart from the ledger
because rows here are posting verdicts, not unique provider calls.

VerdictReachSpend.title: VerdictReachSpend
VerdictReachSpend.description: Whether the work was for a posting anybody could still be shown.

View.title: View
View.description:
One saved view, the same row every route here returns.

`state` stays a free object. It is the page's own request shape and the
API never reads it, so declaring its keys here would be this module
claiming to know a page's vocabulary and going stale the first time a
page grows a filter.

Waste.title: Waste
Waste.description: A diagnostic, not proof that earlier work was unnecessary.

WorkerHeartbeat.title: WorkerHeartbeat
WorkerHeartbeat.description:
The fleet, thinner than /workers: no throughput and no running task,
because this answers "is anybody there" beside the queue numbers.

YearsExperience.title: YearsExperience
YearsExperience.description:
`stated` is how many postings said anything at all. The silent
majority is the finding as often as the stated minority is, which is why
this is a count beside the distribution and not a percentage.
